title: Customer registration and sign-in

sourcesRead.contributes: user story, context (routes, REST base, test data, form fields), AC-1..AC-9, out of scope

actors: prospective ParaBank customer; partner apps authenticating through the banking REST service
context: ParaBank web app at /parabank/; registration page register.htm linked as "Register" under the Customer Login panel; sign-in through the Customer Login panel on the home page; REST service base /parabank/services/bank (XML unless Accept: application/json).

No message is shown for Phone #.

acceptanceCriteria.quote: `GET /login/{username}/{password}` with valid credentials answers 200 and returns the customer: `id`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `address` (`street`, `city`, `state`, `zipCode`) and `phoneNumber`, equal to the values entered at registration. With `Accept: application/json` the body is JSON; without it, XML with a `customer` root element.

rules.text: Registration form fields: First Name, Last Name, Address, City, State, Zip Code, Phone #, SSN, Username, Password, Confirm. Phone # is optional; all other fields are required.
Every check starts by registering its own customer with a fresh, unique user name; the password comes from the environment variable PB_USER_PASSWORD (never hard-coded).

errorModel.body: "First name is required.", "Last name is required.", "Address is required.", "City is required.", "State is required.", "Zip Code is required.", "Social Security Number is required.", "Username is required.", "Password is required.", "Password confirmation is required."

errorModel.body: The username and password could not be verified.

auth.mechanism: UI: user name and password on the Customer Login panel of the home page. REST: user name and password in the path of GET /login/{username}/{password}.
auth.credentials: each check registers its own customer with a fresh, unique user name; password from the environment variable PB_USER_PASSWORD

testData.strategy: every check starts by registering its own customer with a fresh, unique user name (the shared demo database can be reset at any time)
constraints: password from the environment variable PB_USER_PASSWORD, never hard-coded
a fresh, unique user name per check

gaps.element: how an API-layer check creates its customer: the story states that every check registers its own customer, but names only the registration page (register.htm), no REST registration endpoint

tried.result: L25: every check registers its own customer; L23/L26: registration page and its fields; no REST endpoint for registration is named
published API docs (openapi.yaml) list no customer-creation endpoint (only /customers/update/{customerId}, /createAccount for accounts); registration works through register.htm

gaps.value: Customers are created through the registration page register.htm (UI seed wrapped in seed.create); no REST registration endpoint exists. No customer-deletion endpoint exists, so registered customers cannot be cleaned up

gaps.element: Customer Login panel locators (user name and password field labels, sign-in button), Accounts Overview route and how its account numbers are shown

tried.result: L23 names the Customer Login panel on the home page; L37 names the Accounts Overview page and "Log Out"; no field labels, button label or route are given

Customer Login panel inputs have no accessible names; located by input[name=username] / input[name=password]; submit button "Log In". After sign-in the browser lands on overview.htm; account numbers are links in #accountTable

gaps.value: Login panel: input[name="username"], input[name="password"], button "Log In"; Accounts Overview route overview.htm, heading "Accounts Overview"; account numbers: links in #accountTable tbody

gaps.element: exact page/control locators on register.htm (submit button label, where each field message is rendered) and the left-panel element for the greeting and Account Services menu

tried.result: L23 gives the page register.htm and the "Register" link; L26 gives the field labels; no submit button label or message placement beyond "next to each field"

register.htm inputs have no accessible names (labels are table cells); ids customer.firstName … customer.password, repeatedPassword; button "Register"; each field message is rendered in the third cell of the field row; left panel shows "Welcome <first> <last>" text and heading "Account Services"

gaps.value: Inputs by id ([id="customer.firstName"], … [id="customer.password"], [id="repeatedPassword"]); submit button "Register"; message = same table row as the field; greeting text + heading "Account Services" in the left panel

gaps.element: authentication for GET /customers/{id} and GET /customers/{id}/accounts: the story does not say whether these calls need credentials or how they are sent

tried.result: L24 gives the REST base and Accept header only; L40 names the endpoints with no auth scheme
GET /customers/{id} and GET /customers/{id}/accounts answered 200 without credentials, cookies or headers (api-probe chain)

gaps.value: No credentials are sent; both calls take only the customer id in the path

gaps.element: how "the user name cannot sign in afterwards" is observed: the story does not state what GET /login/{username}/{password} (or the Customer Login panel) answers for a user name that was never created

tried.result: L33: "no customer is created (the user name cannot sign in afterwards)"; L39 states 400 only for a wrong password of an existing user; nothing for an unknown user name

gaps.value: Sign-in fails: GET /login/{username}/{password} with that user name and the password used does not answer 200 with a customer. No specific status or message is asserted.

gaps.element: what "returns the same customer" and "returns the account(s) whose numbers are shown" compare: which customer fields, and whether the account set must be equal or only contain the shown numbers

tried.result: L40: "returns the same customer" and "returns the account(s) whose numbers are shown in the Accounts Overview"; no field list or set semantics stated

gaps.value: GET /customers/{id} succeeds and its id, firstName, lastName, address (street, city, state, zipCode) and phoneNumber equal those of the login response (the fields AC-7 lists); the account ids returned by GET /customers/{id}/accounts are exactly the account numbers shown in the Accounts Overview.
